items.informal_name: Linear Sum Identity for Single-Nonzero Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_5} {R₂ : Type u_6} (S : Type u_8) [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : Semiring S] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] {σ : R →+* R₂} [inst_7 : Module S N] [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R₂ S N]
  (f : α → M →ₛₗ[σ] N) (i : α) (m : M), ((Finsupp.lsum S) f) (Finsupp.single i m) = (f i) m
items.informal_description: For any family of $\sigma$-linear maps $f : \alpha \to M \to_\sigma N$, index $i \in \alpha$, and element $m \in M$, the linear sum $\text{lsum} \, f$ evaluated at the finite support function $\text{single}_i(m)$ equals $f(i)(m)$.

items.informal_name: Composition of Finsupp.lsum and lsingle Recovers Original Map
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_5} {R₂ : Type u_6} (S : Type u_8) [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : Semiring S] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] {σ : R →+* R₂} [inst_7 : Module S N] [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R₂ S N]
  (f : α → M →ₛₗ[σ] N) (i : α), (Finsupp.lsum S) f ∘ₛₗ Finsupp.lsingle i = f i
items.informal_description: For any family of σ-linear maps $ f: \alpha \to M \to_\sigma N $ and any index $ i \in \alpha $, the composition of the linear equivalence $ \text{Finsupp.lsum} \, f $ with the single-index embedding $ \text{lsingle}_i $ equals the map $ f(i) $. This establishes that applying the linear sum equivalence followed by the single-index embedding reconstructs the original map at index $ i $.

items.informal_name: Linear Sum Evaluates to Component Map on Single-Element Insertion
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} (S : Type u_4) {M : ι → Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Module R (M i)] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid N]
  [inst_4 : Module R N] [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : Semiring S] [inst_7 : Module S N]
  [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R S N] (F : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N) (i : ι) (x : M i),
  ((DFinsupp.lsum S) F) (DFinsupp.single i x) = (F i) x
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ S $, family of $ S $-modules $ \{M(i)\}_{i \in \iota} $, and another $ S $-module $ N $, given a family of $ S $-linear maps $ F_i : M(i) \to N $, the linear map $ \Phi $ constructed by $ \mathrm{lsum} $ satisfies $ \Phi(\mathrm{single}_i(x)) = F_i(x) $ for any $ x \in M(i) $. This states that applying the linear sum map to a function with a single non-zero element $ x $ at index $ i $ yields the result of the $ i $-th component map applied to $ x $.

                      [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] →
                        [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] →
                          {σ : R →+* R₂} →
                 ...
items.informal_description: The linear equivalence $\text{Finsupp.lsum}$ establishes a bijection between families of $\sigma$-linear maps $\alpha \to M \to_\sigma N$ and $\sigma$-linear maps on finite support functions $\alpha \to_0 M \to_\sigma N$. For a family $F$, the forward direction maps a finite support function $d$ to the sum $\sum_{i \in \text{support } d} F(i)(d(i))$. The inverse direction composes a linear map $F$ with the single-index embedding $\text{lsingle}_i$. The equivalence is proven by verifying additivity, scalar multiplication compatibility, and bijectivity via $\text{lsingle}$ composition.
